import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided by the user
data_str = """amount,is_fraud,transaction_type,hour_of_day
115.02,0,refund,22
44.37,0,payment,5
144.25,0,transfer,21
536.22,0,payment,17
38.43,0,payment,5
"""
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data_str))

# Convert 'is_fraud' to a categorical type with meaningful labels for better plotting
# This ensures that even if only one category is present, the label is clear
df['is_fraud_label'] = df['is_fraud'].map({0: 'Not Fraud', 1: 'Fraud'})

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a figure with three subplots to provide a comprehensive view
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(12, 16), sharex=False)

# Plot 1: Transaction Count by Hour of Day, Differentiated by Fraud Status
# This helps identify if certain hours are more prone to fraud
sns.countplot(data=df, x='hour_of_day', hue='is_fraud_label', palette='viridis', ax=axes[0])
axes[0].set_title('Transaction Count by Hour of Day and Fraud Status', fontsize=15)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Number of Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[0].legend(title='Fraud Status', loc='upper right', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=0) # No rotation needed for a small number of hours
axes[0].grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Plot 2: Transaction Count by Transaction Type, Differentiated by Fraud Status
# This helps identify which transaction types are more frequently associated with fraud
sns.countplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', hue='is_fraud_label', palette='viridis', ax=axes[1])
axes[1].set_title('Transaction Count by Transaction Type and Fraud Status', fontsize=15)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Number of Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[1].legend(title='Fraud Status', loc='upper right', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)
axes[1].grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Plot 3: Distribution of Transaction Amounts by Fraud Status
# This helps understand if fraudulent transactions typically involve different amounts
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='is_fraud_label', y='amount', palette='viridis', ax=axes[2], inner='quartile')
axes[2].set_title('Distribution of Transaction Amounts by Fraud Status', fontsize=15)
axes[2].set_xlabel('Fraud Status', fontsize=12)
axes[2].set_ylabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=12)
axes[2].grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping titles and labels, and add an overall title
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95]) # Adjust rect to make space for suptitle
plt.suptitle('Comprehensive Transaction Analysis: Insights into Fraud', fontsize=18, y=0.99)

# Save the figure to output.png
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300)
